g.title: engine.Sweep runs seeds as parallel jobs (-j) and stops at the first failure unless told to keep going. 200 seeds took 9.4 s on a laptop.
The seed number is the whole bug report. It fixes the scheduling, network, disk and fault streams, so the same seed gives the same failure on any machine.
Reruns the seed and prints the full trace and a determinism hash over every host call. With -html it writes a timeline of messages, faults and the failing check.

ddmin over the fault list, then a capped workload, a trimmed duration and simplified faults, repeated until nothing changes. A candidate is kept only if it fails with the same class, node, property and message.
Saved as .seedfall/seed-N.faults.json. replay, inspect and verify take it with -faults, and seedfall pin keeps it as a regression that later sweeps replay.

Replays the failing schedule against the patched code, double-checking determinism, then sweeps fresh seeds sized for 95 percent confidence and writes a Markdown proof. Optional -mutate also checks that the checks would notice a broken disk.
